L326: cite12†suomiLue artikkeli suomeksi cite13†svenskaLäs artikeln på svenska cite14†English L327: # What is Antarctica — and how does it relate to Finland?
L328: 
L329: Ministry for Foreign Affairs
L330: 
L331: Publication date 12.3.2021 8.25
L332: 
L333: Type:News item
L334: 
L335: Antarctica, located around the geographical South Pole, and the surrounding islands south of 60 degrees South latitude together form the Antarctic region. Antarctica is the coldest, driest and windiest place on earth. It does not belong to any state and has no indigenous or permanent settlement.
L336: cite15†Image: Penguin mother with her chick†um.fi The climate in Antarctica has impact worldwide. Photo: Pixabay
L337: 
L338: What, then, connects Arctic Finland, intersected by the Arctic Circle, to that southernmost continent of our planet? Surprisingly many things. In fact, that barren and almost completely ice-covered continent has an integral connection to every corner of the world. The reason is the continent’s central impact on the global climate and its changes.
L339: ## Changes in ice cover affect the lives of millions around the world
L340: 
L341: Antarctica is covered by a huge ice sheet that in places is almost five kilometres thick. It contains 75% of the entire world’s fresh water and 90% of all the ice. It is therefore easy to see that even slight changes to the continent can have major global impacts.
L342: The scales are huge. Fortunately, complete melting of the Antarctic glacier is unlikely, but if this were to happen, it is estimated that the sea level would rise by about 60 metres. Average temperatures have risen in both polar regions, and according to researchers, the melting of ice in the western part of Antarctica is accelerating at a rate that is difficult to predict. If the whole of West Antarctica were to melt, the estimated rise in the sea level would be about four metres worldwide.
L343: Even a much smaller rise in sea level could affect the lives of millions of people living on the coast around the world.
L344: ## Finland plays an active role in Antarctic research
L345: 
L346: By studying the ice and atmosphere of Antarctica, the mechanism of climate change can be determined and both its rate and the human impact on climate change can be predicted more accurately. Studying the layers of ice can reveal information about the distant past. Antarctic research is, in a way, research on the entire globe and its history and future. The Antarctic is also home to rare, cold and dark ecosystems.
L347: Finland is actively involved in Antarctic research. Finland has its own research station in Antarctica, Aboa, maintained by FINNARP, the Finnish Antarctic research programme of the Finnish Meteorological Institute. Regular research expeditions to Aboa have been organised since the 1980s. Although Finnish researchers would certainly find snow and ice closer to home, the research conducted in Antarctica is unique.
L348: Antarctica has a large, solid continental glacier and its own special features with regard, among others, to temperature, wind and atmospheric humidity. Corresponding information cannot be obtained from research done anywhere else.
L349: Finland conducts extensive cooperation on Antarctic research and logistics. For example, the meteorological institutions of Finland and Argentina have long-term cooperation to study the ozone depletion phenomenon. This includes continuous ozone measurements taken at Marambio, the Argentine research station. Antarctic research done by Finland is coordinated under the Ministry of Education and Culture and is mainly funded by project funding from the Academy of Finland.
L350: cite16†Image: Aboa research station buildings in Antarctica.†um.fi Finland has its own research station in Antarctica, Aboa, maintained by FINNARP, the Finnish Antarctic research programme of the Finnish Meteorological Institute. Photo: Pasi Ylirisku/FINNARP
L351: ## An international agreement protects the Antarctic in many ways
L352: The Antarctic Treaty protects the continent for scientific research. Military activities and mineral excavations for purposes other than research are prohibited. Finland’s long-term research activities have enabled us to gain Consultative Party status of the Antarctic Treaty. The Consultative Parties to the Treaty exercise decision-making power.
L353: It is important that we have a seat at the tables where decisions about Antarctica are made now that the need for information on climate change is continuing to grow. The agreement also aims to protect Antarctica from the impacts of tourism, which grew almost exponentially before the COVID-19 pandemic.
L354: Some interest towards the continent may also stem from strategic considerations, including as regards the exploitation of its natural resources.
L355: ## Finland is a key polar actor
L356: 
L357: What makes Finland a key polar actor is our participation in both the Arctic Council and the Antarctic Treaty. In addition to Finland, only Norway, Sweden, Russia and the United States are decision-making countries in both polar regions.
L358: 
L359: For Finland, Antarctica and the international cooperation conducted there also offer an opportunity to utilise and present our expertise in the cold climate sector.
